content:
Alex: noticed steady memory drift on canary during long-chat load test, looks like KV pages slowly accumulating :eyes:
Maria: logs point to eviction path not decrementing refcounts for some page shards
Alex: which commit/regression window?
Maria: started after the batching refactor ~2026-11-03, repro only with long contexts (>50k tokens)
Cheng: can you paste the trace where alignment is off?
Maria: sure, snippet from runtime.log:
```
[2026-11-18T14:12:03Z] evict: page=0x7f8a3d tag=0x2a refcount=0 but still linked
[2026-11-18T14:12:03Z] append_kv: expected_align=16 expected_offset=10240 wrote_at=10224
[2026-11-18T14:12:03Z] request_id=0x8f3 closed but next_req_ptr=0x7e5 refers to same page
```
Sam: align by 16 off-by-16 is suspicious — sounds like a fragment boundary got shifted when pages stitched after eviction
Cheng: my hypothesis: concurrent eviction+append race. Eviction merges tombstones and updates page headers; append assumes headers stable and uses cached base offsets. If header update wins, append writes with stale base -> misaligned token metadata
Irene: perf profile on canary showed a hotspot in `kv_merge_tombstones` during large responses (flame: https://perf.redwood/abc123) :thinking_face:
Alex: @Cheng can you try a focused reproducer: one request that fills a page, triggers eviction, then immediately appends a continuation that crosses the page boundary
Cheng: working on a repro harness now. quick script to allocate repeated tokens to force page rollover and call eviction path explicitly
Maria: also observed stale block references across requests — next request sometimes sees page index from previous req id. potential cross-request contamination
Sam: I added an assert in `kv_append` to verify alignment and a check to ensure `page->owner_req == current_req` before using cached offsets. running stress tests locally
infra-bot: canary deploy queued (build 0.3.21-canary) :rocket:
Cheng: repro confirmed locally with the harness. Reproducer attached as gist: https://gist.github.com/cheng/repro-kv-epoch-123
Maria: dug into trace: tombstone merge path was holding a write lock, append used relaxed ordering and read stale `page_base` from cache -> mispatch. Fix: fence the base read or bump a generation counter on the page header
Sam: opened PR 8912 with generation-counter approach + alignment assert + unit test that simulates concurrent eviction+append
Irene: running 12h mem-stress on canary with PR applied, will report back on memory growth trend (baseline was +120MB/hour)
Alex: great. Follow-ups: add a metric `kv.pages_in_use_per_req` and a chaos test that toggles eviction frequency during heavy batching to catch regressions earlier
Maria: also backport patch to Dedicated runtime image; long-context customers hit this worst
Alex: thanks everyone. If tests pass, ship to staging then roll canary more broadly.
Sam: noted, will add a check in rollout to monitor page count and allocation rate
Cheng: PR ready for review, added detailed repro notes and a stress harness script
Maria: merging after CI, will watch canary metrics for next 24h
Alex: :thumbsup:
